answer: Each identity runs one island lantern at its tower zenith, locking a 70-credit bond. Each epoch it claims a sighting range, confirmed by two key-signed shore observers at that distance. An auditor recomputes the maximum range from heights with the horizon formula; a claim beyond it, or a single-observer signing, burns the bond. The kth filing costs 36+5(k-1): first 36, 1000th 5031, so 1000 fakes pay 2,533,500 plus 70,000 locked. An honest keeper pays 36 once, reclaiming the bond after an epoch. A rented-lantern ring fails: its flash comes from the owner's zenith, not the claimant's island.
